name: Microsoft Graph Directory
description: Read Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Active Directory users through Microsoft Graph. 2 tools, built-in OAuth2 auth.
instructions:
This connector uses Microsoft Graph API v1.0 directory endpoints with the built-in AnythingMCP OAuth2 authorization-code flow.

**Setup**:
1. Register an app in Microsoft Entra ID at https://portal.azure.com → **App registrations → New registration**.
2. Add a Web redirect URI: `<your SERVER_URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` (for local Docker, usually `http://localhost:4000/api/mcp-oauth/callback`).
3. Create a client secret under **Certificates & secrets**.
4. Add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions: `User.Read`, `User.ReadBasic.All`, `User.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, and `offline_access`. `Directory.Read.All` commonly requires tenant admin consent, but it lets agents fetch richer directory profile fields beyond the basic public profile.
5. Set:
   - `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_TENANT_ID` = your tenant ID, or `organizations`/`common` for broader sign-in
   - `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_CLIENT_ID` = app/client ID
   - `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET` = client secret value
6. Import this adapter, then run the one-time OAuth flow: `POST /api/connectors/{id}/oauth/authorize` → open the returned URL → sign in and consent. AnythingMCP stores the encrypted access/refresh tokens and refreshes them automatically.

**Authentication**: OAuth2. Requests send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` automatically after the OAuth callback succeeds.

**Directory scope**: these tools read users from the signed-in user's tenant. Use `microsoft_graph_directory_list_users` to find directory users, then pass either the Graph user `id` or `userPrincipalName` into `microsoft_graph_directory_get_user_details`.

**Fields**: Microsoft Graph returns its default user projection when `$select` is omitted. Pass `$select` to request fields such as `id`, `displayName`, `mail`, `userPrincipalName`, `jobTitle`, `department`, `accountEnabled`, `businessPhones`, `mobilePhone`, `officeLocation`, `createdDateTime`, or `signInActivity` when your permissions allow them.

**Filtering and search**: Microsoft Graph supports OData `$filter`, `$orderby`, `$search`, and `$count` on `/users`. Advanced queries use the `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` header, which this adapter sends on list requests. `$search` expressions usually look like `"displayName:Alex"` or `"mail:alex"`.

**Pagination**: list calls return OData `@odata.nextLink` when more users exist. Use `$top` to keep responses small; agents should usually request 10-50 users per page.

**Rate limits**: Microsoft Graph throttles per app, tenant, and user. On 429 honor `Retry-After`.

**Out of scope here**: creating/updating/deleting users, groups, app registrations, directory roles, audit logs, delta sync, app-only client-credentials tenant access, and beta-only Entra properties.

tools.name: microsoft_graph_directory_list_users
tools.description: List Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Active Directory users in the tenant. Supports OData $select, $filter, $orderby, $search, $count, $top, and $skipToken for directory discovery workflows.

$top.description: Maximum users to return in one page. Use 10-50 for agent workflows; Graph supports larger pages depending on tenant and query.

$filter.description: OData filter, e.g. accountEnabled eq true or startswith(displayName,'Alex').

$orderby.description: OData order expression, e.g. displayName asc or userPrincipalName asc.

$search.description: Graph search expression, usually quoted, e.g. "displayName:Alex" or "mail:alex". Advanced queries use ConsistencyLevel eventual.

$count.description: When true, include @odata.count. Advanced queries use ConsistencyLevel eventual.

$skipToken.description: Pagination token extracted from a previous @odata.nextLink when continuing a large user list.

tools.name: microsoft_graph_directory_get_user_details
tools.description: Get detailed Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Active Directory user profile data by Graph user ID or userPrincipalName, with optional $select to control returned fields.

userId.description: Microsoft Graph user ID or userPrincipalName, e.g. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 or alex@contoso.com.
